question.text: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> of ice at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>-</mo><mn>20°C</mn></math> is mixed with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> of water at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20°C</mn></math>. The water content of the final mixture is (Latent heat of ice <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>=</mo><mn>80</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi>kcal</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>kg</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>, the specific heat of water <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kcal</mi><msup><mi>kg</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>°</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> and specific heat of ice <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>=</mo><mtext>0.5</mtext><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi>kcal</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><msup><mi>kg</mi><mrow><mo>–</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>°</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mrow><mo>–</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> )

solution.text:
Here, m, s and θ1 are the mass, specific heat and temperature difference for water respectively. Similarly, M, S and θ2 are the corresponding quantities for ice. Here, L is the latent heat of fusion.

We have, the heat lost by water =msθ, heat gained by ice =MSθ+ML.

From the principle of calorimetry, we have, the heat lost by water=heat gained by ice.

Hence, msθ1=MSθ2+ML.

5×1×20-0=2×0.5×20+x×80

x=1 kg

1 kg of ice melts to form water.

Hence, final amount of water 5 kg+1 kg=6 kg.
